standard_prerequisites.name: Nakayama's lemma
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked in the counted proof at line 25218
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the equality f_1 K = K for a finite-length kernel K into K = 0.

standard_prerequisites.name: Permuting an M-regular sequence
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked in the counted proof at line 25228
standard_prerequisites.use: Upgrades the regularity on the quotient to regularity of the pair g, f_1 on M.

core_obligations: Base case d = 1: show that the kernel of multiplication by g has support the closed point, hence finite length, so that injectivity of f_1 on it forces it to vanish by Nakayama, and check that the quotient is Cohen-Macaulay of depth zero (proof lines 25213-25220).

Induction step: observe that g is still good for the quotient by f_1, apply the induction hypothesis, and use the permutation of a regular sequence to conclude that g, f_1 is M-regular and that the tail is regular on M/gM (proof lines 25223-25231).
proof_roadmap: Settle the one-dimensional case by a support and Nakayama argument (proof lines 25209-25221).
Descend along f_1 and permute the resulting regular sequence (proof lines 25222-25232).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a good element g with respect to a tuple (M, f_1, ..., f_d) is a nonzerodivisor on M and that M/gM is Cohen-Macaulay with maximal regular sequence f_1, ..., f_{d-1} (statement lines 25201-25207). The proof does not rework the definition of goodness: in the case d = 1 it bounds the support of the kernel of multiplication by g to the closed point, so that the kernel has finite length and Nakayama kills it; in general it observes that g stays good on M/f_1M, applies the induction hypothesis, and permutes the resulting regular sequence with f_1 (proof lines 25209-25232). Recognising that the hypothesis descends to the quotient by f_1 is what makes the induction work. H2.
